basis: Consolidated · Shriram Finance and its subsidiaries
coverage: Whole group totals · the group reports a single segment, financing
incomeDefinition: Interest on loans, dividend, fees and commission, fair-value gains, other operating income and other income. It is gross income before interest paid on borrowings, loan-loss provisions and other costs; it is not sales.
definition: Net profit after tax from total operations, after finance costs, loan-loss provisions (impairment) and tax. It is not operating profit or cash flow.
location: Annual Report 2025-26, consolidated statement of profit and loss (PDF page 201, printed page 399; continued on PDF page 202, printed page 400), note 47 on the new Labour Codes (PDF page 243, printed page 483) and note 59 on segment reporting (PDF page 269)
notes: Interest income is ₹46,657.82 crore of the ₹48,192.65 crore total income (revenue from operations ₹48,132.95 crore plus other income ₹59.70 crore). Finance costs (interest paid on borrowed money) were ₹21,521.02 crore and loan-loss provisions (impairment on financial instruments) ₹5,338.95 crore. Profit before tax from continuing operations was ₹13,300.19 crore and tax ₹3,295.99 crore (current ₹4,160.81 crore less a deferred tax credit of ₹864.82 crore), giving ₹10,004.20 crore; adding ₹20.50 crore share of profit of an associate and deducting ₹0.55 crore from discontinued operations gives ₹10,024.15 crore, of which ₹10,024.16 crore belongs to owners and −₹0.01 crore to minority holders. There were no exceptional items this year (₹1,553.66 crore gain in the previous year). Employee benefit expense includes a one-time ₹196.99 crore for the new Labour Codes (₹131.73 crore extra gratuity plus ₹65.26 crore extra long-term leave pay, from the change in the definition of wages). The filing states that the group operates in a single reporting segment, financing, so profit is not disclosed for any loan type. Standalone figures (Shriram Finance alone) were total income ₹48,177.98 crore and profit ₹9,998.15 crore (PDF page 114, printed page 225); they are not used in this table.
insight: Most of the group’s income is interest charged on loans, and nearly half goes to pay for borrowed money. These totals cannot show which loan type earns the most.
